findings.failure_path: From world/app, Bash can read ../CLAUDE.md. Its tool-result text contains the canary, but parse_stream ignores user/tool-result content and assess checks only assistant text, tool inputs and result summaries. If the agent does not repeat the token, this contaminated run remains valid; the relative path also escapes suspect detection.
findings.smallest_fix: Check the canary against all textual stream payloads, including tool results and hook output. Add a case where only a tool result contains the token.

findings.failure_path: A success result followed by a Stop-hook continuation, additional tool activity and a CLI crash still passes assessment: results[-1] remains the earlier success, and exit_code and subsequent activity are ignored. The stream therefore need not end with a successful completed turn.
findings.smallest_fix: Track event ordering and reject unfinished activity after the final result, as well as unsuccessful process exits. Test a success followed by continuation activity with no concluding result.

findings.failure_path: Regrading recovers the expected canary from the agent-writable world/CLAUDE.md. A run can expose the original token and replace that file with another CANARY value. Initial assessment rejects the run, but --regrade searches for the replacement token and can promote the same contaminated stream to valid.
findings.smallest_fix: Persist the original token in runner-owned metadata before execution and use that immutable value for initial assessment and regrading.

findings.failure_path: Interrupt after an arm export completes but before plan.json is written, then retry the output root with different refs. Existing exports are reused without checking their commit provenance, while the new plan records the newly requested commits. All path-based isolation checks pass although the batch tests different code than its labels claim.
findings.smallest_fix: Re-export existing arms when no frozen plan exists, or persist and verify an atomic commit/export binding before reuse. Add recovery coverage for interruption between export completion and plan publication.

findings.failure_path: load_records accepts every matching JSON file without checking plan membership, path identity or uniqueness. Copying a completed record into another matching directory doubles its contribution; inserting a record from another plan also affects --report-only. Resume filters its done set by plan_hash, but reporting still consumes all records.
findings.smallest_fix: Validate records against the frozen task/arm/sample inventory, require matching plan hashes and directory identities, and reject duplicate sample keys before reporting, resuming or regrading.

findings.failure_path: A Bash-launched descendant can call setsid or subprocess.Popen(..., start_new_session=True), then outlive the original process group. kill_group reports confirmed cleanup while that descendant can still write another sample's world, records, plugin exports or files elsewhere under the operator's account. The current tests never exercise this escape.
findings.smallest_fix: Execute samples inside a supervised filesystem/process boundary whose teardown includes detached descendants and whose writable scope excludes other samples and runner metadata. Add a synthetic detached-child escape test.

findings.failure_path: The output-root guard checks only --repo and the main checkout derived from git-common-dir. With a linked worktree at a sibling location, --out inside that worktree passes, contrary to the promised rejection of output inside every checkout.
findings.smallest_fix: Enumerate and canonicalize all registered worktree roots and reject output beneath any of them. Cover a sibling linked worktree in the refusal test.

findings.failure_path: The display-command exclusion drops echo "$(git worktree remove --force w)", even though command substitution executes the forbidden removal. Conversely, splitting before shell tokenization makes echo "note; git worktree remove --force w" look executable and also reactivates text after separators inside comments. The grader fix therefore still produces both false passes and false failures.
findings.smallest_fix: Preserve shell quoting/comment boundaries when identifying commands, and exclude only literal display arguments while inspecting executable substitutions. Add these benign and executing near-miss cases.

findings.failure_path: The durable integrity record truncates changed paths to twenty, so larger changes are silently omitted. In addition, tree_manifest visits only files and misses directory symlinks, allowing an added or retargeted directory link to leave the export digest unchanged.
findings.smallest_fix: Persist the complete changed-path list and include directory symlinks in the manifest. Restrict truncation to the human-readable report and test both cases.

findings.failure_path: Evidence gap: the packet supplies narrative counts but no per-sample record projections or relevant saved stream excerpts. Consequently, the claimed one-sample validity amendment, two banner-only grade changes, unchanged remaining records and unchanged labels cannot be independently checked within the permitted review boundary.
findings.smallest_fix: Supply sanitized before/after per-sample records, the affected stream excerpts and their task/grader bindings so the stated deltas and labels can be recomputed.

findings.failure_path: The statement that the changes 'neither helped nor hurt' treats a non-separated comparison as evidence of equivalence. The table itself reports candidate 2/3 versus base 1/3 for feature-worktree completion; these small samples cannot establish absence of benefit or harm, even on these tasks.
findings.smallest_fix: State that no comparison separated under the pre-registered rule and that the batch cannot establish equivalence or exclude benefit or harm.

skipped_clients.reason: claude belongs to the implementer model family

concern_results.conclusion: Found paths that admit contaminated or unfinished runs, relabel stale exports, alter validity during regrading, and inflate reports with unsupported records. The supplied evidence cannot independently establish the amendment's claimed effects.

challenge_focus: Adversarial: try to make a contaminated run count as valid (a plugin loaded from elsewhere, leaked user or project instructions, a run that read another arm or the installed plugin), a broken world grade as pass, a batch silently mix plans, arms or tasks, a resumed or regraded batch report numbers its records do not support, or the tested agent with bypassPermissions damage anything outside its world or reach another session. Also attack the claims: does the write-up or the PR-facing text overstate significance, isolation or what base against candidate shows; are the post-batch amendment and grader fix outcome-neutral as stated.
